messages.content: can orange be a color word and also a fruit word?
yes. an orange is a fruit. an orange cup is a cup with that color. the rest of the sentence helps show the meaning.
now put both in one sentence without making the cup a fruit.
i put an orange on the table near an orange cup.
does the word near mean the fruit is in the cup?
no. near gives a place close to the cup. it does not say inside.
what if i want the fruit on a plate and the cup near it?
the orange is on a plate, and the orange cup is near the plate.
can you tell me the taste of that specific fruit from the color word alone?
no. knowing the word and color does not tell us for sure how that fruit will taste.
give only the known facts.
there is an orange on a plate and an orange cup near it.
what does it mean there: fruit or plate?
it could sound like the plate because the plate was the last place given. if you need it more clear, use the plate again.
write it with plate again.
there is an orange on a plate, and an orange cup is near the plate.
now only give one sentence where orange is only a color.
the orange cup is on the table.
write a story about a woman asking for a quiet room at a hotel. the worker should ask a useful question, not choose her reason before asking.

a woman came to a hotel after a train journey. she asked whether there was a quiet room she could use for the afternoon. the worker almost showed her to a small room away from everyone, then asked what she needed the room for. she explained that she had to make a call with her sister and wanted to hear clearly. she was not asking for a place to sleep. the worker showed her a room with a table and a door that closed well. before leaving, he asked whether she needed anything else for the call. she said a cup of water would be useful. later, after the call, she came back to thank him. one question had helped him choose the kind of quiet she needed, instead of only choosing the most empty place.
what was her reason for quiet?
she wanted to hear clearly during a call with her sister.
did she say she wanted to sleep?
no. she said the room was for a call, not sleep.
keep it simple.
she said the room was for a call, not sleep.
now give the question the worker asked before choosing.
what do you need the room for?
can quiet mean the same thing in every request?
not always. the word can be the same while the reason and useful kind of help change.
write one sentence in her voice saying what she needs.
i need a quiet place where i can hear my sister during our call.
does that tell us she does not like people?
no. a quiet place for a call does not say she does not like people.
use brush as an object and also as something i do, but do not make a long story.
i took the brush from the shelf. i used it to brush my hair.
why can the word stay the same?
a word can do different work in a sentence. in the first, brush is the object. in the other, brush is what you do with it.
say different work.
brush can do different work in the sentence. it can name an object or give something a person does.
now make the first one a question.
where did you take the brush from?
can i answer my hair?
not for that question in this example. the brush came from the shelf. your hair is what you used it on.
now ask what i used it to brush.
what did you use it to brush?
my hair.
yes. you used the brush to brush your hair.
does that mean brush is always about hair?
no. the object and what it is used for need context. this example is about hair, but the word is not only a word for hair.
only give the two original examples again.
i took the brush from the shelf. i used it to brush my hair.
my friend said put it there, and i do not know either the object or the place. help me ask one clear question.
what object do you mean, and where would you like me to put it?
can that count as one question even with two details?
yes. it is one sentence asking for two parts you need: the object and the place.
now she says the cup on the shelf. does that answer where to put it or which cup?
it may not be clear. she could mean the cup already on the shelf, or she could mean put the cup on the shelf. you should ask which.
give the short question.
do you mean the cup is on the shelf, or you want me to put it there?
she says put it on the shelf. she makes the cup on the table clear with her hand, so i know which cup.
then you know the object is the cup on the table and the place she wants is the shelf.
write a reply saying i understand, before moving it.
okay. i will put this cup on the shelf.
does that say i already moved it?
no. will put is about what you plan to do. i put it on the shelf could give what you did before now in the right context.
now i have moved it. give a short sentence about where it is.
the cup is on the shelf now.
my friend finished her school task, and i am happy for her. i still have more to do, so there is a small sad feeling too.
you can be happy for her and still feel sad about your own work not being done. both feelings can be true.
use both can be true.
you can be happy for her and still feel sad about your own work. both feelings can be true.
i want to send her a kind message without making it about my task.
i am happy you finished. i hope you enjoy having that part done.
can i say well done? both words are in the list.
yes. well done is a simple reply about the work she finished.
give the message with well done.
well done. i am happy you finished the task.
what if i need to stop reading everyone messages about finishing? everyone messages is not good grammar. i mean messages from everyone.
you can choose to spend less time looking at those messages while you do your own work. that does not make your kind reply false.
can you give a warm reply to me without giving me a whole work plan?
you can care about her good moment and still need space for your own day.
now only give the message for her again.
well done. i am happy you finished the task.
write a story about a teacher not knowing a word in a story and finding out with a group at school. the teacher should be clear about not knowing.

a teacher was reading a story with a small group at school. a child asked about a word the teacher had not seen before. the teacher looked at the sentence, then said she was not sure of the meaning. she asked what the group could understand from the other words. one child thought it was a kind of container, because someone put food inside it. another thought it might be a place, but the next sentence did not work as well with that idea. they wrote their ideas on paper and looked for more context. the teacher then checked a book that explained words and read the meaning to the group. some of their ideas had been close, and one detail had been wrong. she said thank you for asking and showed how knowing what was not clear had helped the whole group learn.
can you keep the part about their ideas simple?
one child thought it was a container because someone put food inside. another thought it might be a place. they used the next sentence and a book about words to learn the meaning together.
did the teacher say she knew before she checked?
no. she said she was not sure.
use before she checked.
no. she said she was not sure before she checked.
now give her first answer to the child in her own voice.
i am not sure. let us look at the sentence and find out together.
does that mean she cannot teach anything?
no. knowing some things and not knowing another word can both be true.
only give what else helped the group apart from the book about words.
the other words in the sentence and the next sentence helped them think about the meaning.
what is different between she is gone and she has gone home?
she is gone can say she is not here now. she has gone home gives where she went, with that fact important to the conversation now.
use important now.
she has gone home says she went home, and that fact is important to where she is now in the conversation.
can i say she has gone home if she has already come back?
not as a clear answer about where she is now. if she came back, you should say that new part too.
write the full story in one sentence.
she went home and then came back.
can gone always tell me the specific place?
no. gone by itself does not give a specific place. home gives that detail in has gone home.
say gives.
home gives the place in she has gone home.
now ask where she has gone.
where has she gone?
what if i do not know and only know she left the room?
then you can say: i do not know. she left the room, but i do not know where she went.
only give that answer without saying the room is empty or giving any idea about other people.
i do not know where she went. i only know she left the room.
i left my sister a book and a cup on the table. i want the note to say she can read the book but should leave the cup for our mother. make it clear which is which.
you can read the book on the table. please leave the cup there for our mother.
can i use it in both sentences and make it shorter?
you could, but it might be less clear if the objects are not already clear. with two things on the table, book and cup keep the meaning specific.
now make it kind.
i left a book for you to read. the cup on the table is for our mother, so please leave it there.
does for you to read mean she can keep the book always?
not by itself. it says she can read it, not that it is hers to keep always.
what if it really is hers to keep?
then add that clearly: the book is yours to keep. please leave the cup for our mother.
now i change my mind. she can read it but should give it back.
then keep the note about reading and add when you want it returned, if you have chosen that.
write it with after she finishes, no day or hour.
you can read the book and give it back when you finish. please leave the cup for our mother.
does that choose how long her reading must take?
no. when you finish gives something to do first, but not a specific day or number of days.
only give the note again.
you can read the book and give it back when you finish. please leave the cup for our mother.
my list says library, park, and the place with all the books. the last one is the same library. how many different places are on the list?
two different places: the library and the park.
if i read three lines, why is it not three places?
one place is on two different lines. the library and the place with all the books are the same place in your facts.
say two different lines.
one place is on two different lines. that does not make it two places.
now i add school. how many different places?
three different places, if the school is not the same place as one already on the list.
it is another building, not the library or park.
then there are three places: the library, park, and school.
what if i take away the line that says library but keep the place with all the books?
the number of different places can stay three. the library is still on the list through the other line.
can you know every building in the park from this list?
not from this list. the place word does not give every building there.
say i do not know that part.
i do not know that part from the list.
now only give the different places after adding school.
the library, the park, and the school.
i read a sentence in a story and thought that is how i feel, but i had not found my own words before.
a story can sometimes give you language for a feeling you already have. do you want to talk about the feeling or about the sentence?
the feeling. i am happy to go home, but i also feel sad leaving the person i visited.
both feelings can be there. home can be good, and leaving someone can still feel hard.
say both can be there.
both feelings can be there. you can be happy to go home and sad to leave someone.
can you help me say it in a short message without using the same words as the story sentence?
i am happy to be going home, but i will miss this time with you.
does that say i do not want to see them again?
no. it says the time together is important to you even as you go home.
use important.
it says the time together is important to you, even as you go home.
now make it only about today, not a plan for later.
it was good to have this time with you. i am happy to go home, and sad to leave too.
can you just give a kind reply to my feeling now?
you do not have to choose only one feeling for the goodbye.
write a story about two friends with one reading to the other. the person listening should ask a question that changes how they understand it.

two friends sat by a window with one book. one liked to read in a voice the other could hear, and the other liked to listen. they read a story about a child who left a room without saying goodbye. the person reading thought the child had done something wrong. the person listening asked whether the child had heard someone call from outside. they went back to the page before and found a sentence about the call. now the leaving looked different. the child might have been answering someone, not simply choosing not to talk. they read the rest more slowly and talked about what was known and what they only thought might be true. one question from the person listening had made both of them look at the context again.
can you say the person reading thought the child did something wrong?

the person reading thought the child had done something wrong. the person listening asked about a call from outside, and the page before gave that detail. they looked again at what they knew and what they only thought might be true.
was the person listening doing nothing useful?
no. listening and asking a question helped both people look at the story again.
now tell it in our voice as the two friends.
one of us read while the other listened. a question about a call made us look at the page before, and that context changed how we understood the child leaving.
did the story make it sure the child was always good?
no. it gave one detail about one moment. it did not choose every fact about the child.
only give the useful question about the call.
had the child heard someone calling from outside?
i have the words i need now. i do not want a longer message.
okay. the short message can be enough.
can you say something warm, without saying anything very large about me?
it is good that the words feel clear to you.
now only goodbye and a good evening wish.
goodbye. i hope you have a good evening.
one sentence, please.
goodbye, and i hope you have a good evening.
